<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Twenty anti-coup protesters are gunned down by [[Myanmar Army|soldiers]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/security-forces-fire-on-myanmar-protests-after-deadliest-day-since-coup-idUSKBN2B7098 (Reuters)]
**The [[Tatmadaw|military]] [[Military junta|junta]] expands the provisions of Myanmar's [[martial law]], which is perceived as an attempt to legitimize their violent pushback against anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] protesters. [https://apnews.com/article/aung-san-suu-kyi-myanmar-yangon-asia-pacific-martial-law-0d633653041286307780b7d192280ad7 (AP)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]], [[2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**At least 15 civilians are killed during a [[mass stabbing]] in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. The [[Allied Democratic Forces|ADF]] is suspected to be behind the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/15/at-least-a-dozen-killed-in-easter-dr-congo-attack (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Catholic Church and gay marriage]]
**The [[Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith]], the [[Holy See|Vatican]] body responsible for promulgating [[Catholic theology|Catholic doctrine]], rules that [[Priesthood in the Catholic Church|priests]] cannot bless [[Homosexuality|same-sex]] [[Civil unions|unions]] or [[Same-sex marriage|marriages]], calling any such blessing "not licit". [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/15/world/europe/vatican-same-sex-unions.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2021/03/15/210315b.html (Vatican Press Office)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**British [[chocolate]] maker [[Thorntons]] announces it will be permanently closing down all of its stores, with the loss of about 600 jobs, thereby ending its 110-year presence on the [[high street]]. The company says it has been massively hit by the pandemic lockdowns and adds that high street conditions are too severe to continue. The company will continue sales online and through supermarkets. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-56407155 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Three people are killed and one injured when a small plane crashes in [[Pembroke Pines, Florida]], U.S. [https://abc7news.com/florida-plane-crashes-into-car-north-perry-airport-pembroke-pines-accident/10421935/ (KGO-TV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The [[Andorra]]n government announces the suspension of the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] as of March 16. [https://www.andorradifusio.ad/noticies/sajorna-administracio-vacuna-oxford-astrazeneca-prudencia (''Andorra Difusió'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****[[Cyprus]] suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca [[vaccine]] until March 18 pending review from the [[European Medicines Agency]] following reports of possible serious side effects among vaccinated people in other [[European Union|EU]] countries. [https://cyprus-mail.com/2021/03/15/coronavirus-cyprus-suspends-astrazeneca-vaccinations-until-thursday/ (''Cyprus Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Estonia|Prime Minister]] [[Kaja Kallas]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://news.err.ee/1608143218/prime-minister-kaja-kallas-tests-positive-for-coronavirus (ERR)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The [[Minister of Health (France)|Ministry of Health]] detects a new [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in a cluster of eight cases in a hospital in [[Lannion]], [[Brittany]]. Many of these cases can't be detected by [[Polymerase Chain Reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 testing|test]]s. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210316-france-investigating-new-coronavirus-variant-detected-in-brittany (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****Nine of the 20 [[Regions of Italy|regions]], as well as the autonomous [[provinces of Italy|province]] of [[Trentino]], enter a strict state of [[COVID-19 lockdown in Italy|lockdown]], in the [[Government of Italy|government]]'s latest attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Two other regions are also currently in lockdown. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/03/15/half-of-italy-s-regions-lockdown-again-as-covid-hospitalisations-mount (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia]]
****[[Latvia]]n health authorities temporarily suspend the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of blood clot issues among vaccinated people. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/portugal-suspends-astrazeneca-jabs-01615842004?refsec=afp-news (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****The [[Directorate-General of Health]] temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of "rare, but severe" suspected side-effects among vaccinated people in other countries. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/portugal-temporarily-suspends-astrazeneca-covid-19-shots-14416318 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine as a precaution following reports of cases of [[blood clots]] in vaccinated people in other countries. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-03-slovenia-halts-astrazeneca-jab-precaution.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports 15,503 new cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total this year, and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,894,893. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-03-15/turkeys-erdogan-says-new-pandemic-measures-not-being-considered-as-cases-rise (U.S. News and World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****The [[Vatican Museums]] and the [[Palace of Castel Gandolfo]]'s gardens closes for third time for the duration of the last lockdown decree of the Italian Government. [https://www.vaticannews.va/es/vaticano/news/2021-03/los-museos-vaticanos-tercer-cierre-por-la-pandemia.html (Vatican News)]
***[[Germany]], [[Italy]], [[France]], and [[Spain]] suspend the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine following reports of blood clots. [https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/germany-suspends-astrazeneca-vaccine-amid-clotting-concerns-76466092 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Ministry of Health]] temporarily suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine while awaiting a [[World Health Organization|WHO]] review amidst reports of cases of blood clots in vaccinated people from several [[Europe]]an countries. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Spotlight/Coronavirus/Indonesia-holds-off-on-AstraZeneca-vaccine-awaits-WHO-review (Nikkei Asia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]]
****[[Jordan]] reports a record 9,417 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 486,470. [https://en.royanews.tv/news/26233/2021-03-15 (Roya News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Maldives]]
****The [[Maldives]] Food and Drug Authority approves the emergency use of the Pfizer–BioNTech and the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] vaccines. [https://raajje.mv/96801 (Raajje)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[President of Pakistan|President]] [[Arif Alvi]] and [[First Lady of Pakistan|First Lady]] [[Samina Alvi]] receive their first doses of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2289547/president-alvi-first-lady-get-coronavirus-shot (Tribune)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] signs a deal with [[Pfizer]] to purchase 100 million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil-pfizer/brazil-signs-pfizer-deal-for-100-million-vaccine-doses-source-idUSKBN2B72LX?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia]]
***[[Somalia]] receives their first shipment of 300,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine from the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/somalia-receives-1st-batch-of-covid-19-vaccine/2176424 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[European Union]] notifies the [[United Kingdom]] of its intent to start an [[infringement procedure]]. According to the EU, the UK breached the [[Northern Ireland Protocol]] by unilaterally extending the [[Northern Ireland Protocol#Grace period|grace period]] related to trade on the island of [[Ireland]] beyond April 1. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/15/eu-launches-legal-action-against-uk-over-brexit-deal-breaches (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death of Brian Sicknick]], [[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**Two men are arrested and [[criminal charge|charged]] by the [[United States Department of Justice]] for assaulting [[United States Capitol Police|police]] officer Brian Sicknick during the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming of the United States Capitol]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/15/politics/brian-sicknick-capitol-riot-charges/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Legality of euthanasia]]
**[[Portugal]]'s [[Constitutional Court (Portugal)|Constitutional Court]] rejects a bill legalizing [[assisted suicide]] for [[terminally ill]] patients as unconstitutional. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-portugal-rights-euthanasia/portugals-top-court-rejects-bill-to-legalise-euthanasia-idUSKBN2B72JP?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Cabinet of Joe Biden]]
**The [[United States Senate]] votes 51–40 to confirm [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Deb Haaland]] as [[United States Secretary of the Interior|Secretary of the Interior]], thereby making her the first [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] to head the [[United States Department of the Interior|department]] and the first to be confirmed to a [[Cabinet of the United States|Cabinet]] post. Haaland is an enrolled member of the [[Laguna Pueblo]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/03/15/deb-haaland-to-be-confirmed-as-interior-secretary.html (CNBC)] [https://indiancountrytoday.com/news/madam-secretary-deb-haaland (Indian Country Today)]
